methods.label: Rationalize and compare with the midpoints
methods.explanation:
Multiplying by the conjugate turns the small difference into a quotient whose denominator is near \(16\). Let
\[
d=\sqrt{65}-\sqrt{63},
\qquad s=\sqrt{65}+\sqrt{63}>0.
\]
The difference-of-squares identity gives
\[
d=\frac{65-63}{\sqrt{65}+\sqrt{63}}=\frac2s.
\]
This suggests \(d\) is near \(2/16=0.125\), exactly halfway between \(0.12\) and \(0.13\), so we must determine which side it lies on.

Because \(4095<64^2\),
\[
s^2=128+2\sqrt{4095}<128+128=256.
\]
Since \(s>0\), this implies \(s<16\), and therefore \(d>2/16=0.125\).

For an upper bound, \(\sqrt{65}>8\) and \(\sqrt{63}>7\), so \(s>15\). Hence
\[
0.125<d<\frac2{15}<0.135.
\]
The numbers \(0.125\) and \(0.135\) are the midpoints separating \(0.13\) from its neighboring choices. Thus the closest choice is \(\boxed{0.13}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
